articles.title: Hunting for Beauty’s Biological Signature in the Brain
articles.summary: At Florence’s Galileo Museum, neuroscientists are wiring up volunteers to track brain waves, heartbeats, and sweat as they gaze at Renaissance instruments. Their goal: to find a quantifiable, biological footprint of aesthetic experience.

articles.title: A Quantum Thermometer for Living Cells Could Revolutionize Disease Diagnosis
articles.summary: Japanese researchers have built a uniform, biocompatible quantum sensor that measures temperature inside living cells with high precision. Tested in cancer cells, the molecular spin sensor could one day help diagnose diseases by detecting tiny thermal changes.

articles.title: A Shower Remodel Inspired a Cleaner, Cheaper Way to Extract Lithium
articles.summary: MIT researchers have developed a low-temperature, weak-acid process to extract lithium from silicate ore, slashing costs and carbon emissions. The technique, now being commercialized by startup Rock Zero, could make lithium cheaper than $6,000 per ton.
